rounds.text: Sanghvi Movers Ltd is displaying exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum, underlined by a compounded sales growth of 37% over 5 years and 30% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16], alongside a compounded profit growth of 57% over 5 years [E17]. This robust operational expansion is translating into superior capital efficiency, with the company delivering a ROCE of 14.59% and an ROE of 14.06% that easily outpace sector benchmarks of 6.52% and 4.85% respectively [E9, E10]. Valuation metrics further support a compelling entry point, as a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 934 per share against a market price of Rs 442, offering a substantial margin of safety of 52.7% [E41, E42]. Adding to this disconnect between price and fundamental reality, a reverse DCF indicates that today's market price implies a modest earnings growth of only 7.7%, which sits well below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E43]. Furthermore, institutional money flow registers a positive signal alongside a rules-based screen scoring 94 out of 100 with high confidence [E40, E58], supported by sector tailwinds where the services sector tailwind score stands at +0.59 [E65]. Conceded: [E31].

The bull case relies heavily on strong historical sales and profit growth, but this glosses over significant structural deterioration in operating margins [E25, E27]. The operating margin has dropped to 36% in the trailing twelve months down from 56% three years earlier, representing a sharp 20 percentage point compression, with the yearly trend consistently decreasing over the last four years [E25, E27]. Furthermore, free cash flow has turned deeply negative to minus 130 crore rupees in March 2026, driven by a aggressive surge in borrowings up to 674 crore rupees from 438 crore rupees a year prior [E31, E35]. Compounding these financial strains, filed statements flag a concerning negative note that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E57]. Institutional support is also quietly fading, evidenced by a reduction in domestic institutional holdings from 1.77% down to 1.40% [E39]. Finally, investors must contend with extreme historical volatility and vulnerability, highlighted by a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of 88.3% and an annualized volatility rate touching 48.9% [E49, E50]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong profit growth of 57.2% CAGR over the last five years and maintains a positive cash conversion ratio of 1.51x [E29, E56].
